title: Set-valued models of a small finite-limit theory are locally finitely presentable
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $T$ be a $\mathcal U$-small category with all finite limits, and let $\operatorname{Lex}(T,\mathbf{Set}_{\mathcal U})$ be the category of functors preserving finite limits, with natural transformations as morphisms. A limit is a terminal cone and a finite limit is one indexed by a finite category; colimits have the dual universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This category has all $\mathcal U$-small limits and colimits and is locally finitely presentable: there is a $\mathcal U$-small family of objects $P$ such that each $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves filtered colimits and every object is a filtered colimit of members of this family. Limits and filtered colimits of these models are computed pointwise in sets. Here filtered means nonempty, every two objects have a common receiving object, and every parallel pair of arrows is equalized by a further arrow. Equivalently the same conclusions hold for models of any small finite-limit sketch, a small diagram of sorts and operations with specified finite cones required to be limit cones, by passing to its free finite-limit completion.

source.place: G. M. Kelly, Structures defined by finite limits in the enriched context, I (1982), Sections 4 and 9, especially (9.3), (9.4), (9.7), Theorem (9.8), printed pp. 35–36; specialize the base to Set. The sketch formulation uses the free finite-limit completion in (9.3). Read online; not archived. No Stacks tag states this general sketch theorem.

proof.text: Form a finite-limit sketch $S_T$ with underlying category $T$ and with every finite limit cone in $T$ specified. This is small: finite index categories can be encoded using finite sets of objects and arrows; for each such code, diagrams and cones in the small category $T$ form a small set. Taking their union still gives a $\mathcal U$-small set. Include the empty index category. By the definition of a sketch model in [lem-coef-finite-limit-sketch-models], a model of $S_T$ is exactly a functor $T\to\mathbf{Set}_{\mathcal U}$ preserving finite limits. Both categories have all natural transformations between these functors as morphisms, so their full subcategories of the functor category coincide.

source.place: Kelly (1982), Section 9, (9.2), (9.4), (9.7), Theorem (9.8); elementary theory-to-sketch specialization using the existing general sketch-model node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-finite-limit-sketch-models] to the small sketch $S_T$. Its statement gives all $\mathcal U$-small limits and colimits and a $\mathcal U$-small family of models whose Hom functors preserve $\mathcal U$-small filtered colimits and from which every model is a $\mathcal U$-small filtered colimit. Under the equality of full subcategories in step 1 these are the required objects and universal properties in $\operatorname{Lex}(T,\mathbf{Set}_{\mathcal U})$. The same cited statement gives pointwise limits and filtered colimits. The identification in step 1 leaves every value at $t\in T$ and every natural transformation unchanged, so these pointwise formulas are exactly the formulas asserted for $\operatorname{Lex}$.

source.place: Kelly (1982), Section 9, (9.2), (9.4), (9.7), Theorem (9.8); elementary theory-to-sketch specialization using the existing general sketch-model node.

proof.text: For the final formulation, let $S$ be any small finite-limit sketch as in the statement. This is precisely a small category with a small family of specified finite cones, so it satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-coef-finite-limit-sketch-models] directly. That node supplies the same completeness, cocompleteness, finite-presentability family, and pointwise limit and filtered-colimit conclusions for its models. Thus the sketch formulation follows directly as well; no free-completion theorem is needed in this proof. In the statement the free finite-limit completion is understood as a completion of the sketch respecting its specified cones, not the free completion of its underlying category with those conditions forgotten.

source.place: Kelly (1982), (10.1) and Theorem (10.2), printed p. 40, independently verify the sketch formulation and cone-respecting theory completion. The proof step itself directly applies the existing DAG statement lem-coef-finite-limit-sketch-models.
